items.label: Name
items.tooltip: Used for state IDs and Loxone VI names — must be unique across the camera list.

items.label: Ch
items.tooltip: Channel index — 0 for standalone cameras, 0-15 for NVR channels

items.label: Gate
items.tooltip: Brief WhiteLed flash (≤3 s ON→OFF) from the Reolink app triggers a gate_trigger event to Loxone. Camera user must have Admin role.

items.label: Doorbell
items.tooltip: Mark this camera as a doorbell. Forces visitor/doorbell capability on (some firmware misreports GetDoorbell). Visitor events arrive via webhook push and are sent to <prefix>_<cam>_Visitor as a 1 s pulse.

items.label: NVR
items.tooltip: Mark this row as a Reolink NVR (e.g. RLN8-410). ReoLox pulls the channel list from the device on startup and creates per-channel sub-states under reolox.0.<nvr>.chN.*

items.label: → Loxone
items.tooltip: Send events from this camera/NVR to the Loxone bridge. Disable for NVR rows when standalone cameras already cover the same channels — keeps state tree in ioBroker but stops duplicate Virtual Inputs.

_cameraHelp.text: ℹ️  WhiteLed / spotlight control requires the camera user account to have **Admin** role (not Guest). Change it in the camera Device Settings → User Management. Camera passwords are stored encrypted in the adapter native settings.

defaultPollInterval.label: Default poll interval (seconds)
defaultPollInterval.help: Fallback interval for cameras with no custom interval set

capabilityCacheTtlHours.label: Capability cache TTL (hours)
capabilityCacheTtlHours.help: GetAbility responses are cached on disk to speed up restarts. Set to 0 to disable.

loxoneEnabled.label: Enable Loxone integration
loxoneEnabled.help: Forward camera events directly to Loxone Miniserver (HTTP Virtual Inputs or UDP)

loxoneUser.label: Username
loxoneUser.tooltip: Loxone user with permission to write Virtual Inputs

loxonePassword.label: Password
loxonePassword.tooltip: Stored encrypted in the instance native settings

loxoneAuth.label: Authentication
loxoneAuth.help: Token auth avoids sending the password on every event. Falls back to Basic automatically if the Miniserver does not support it.

loxoneViPrefix.label: Virtual Input prefix
loxoneViPrefix.help: Prefix for all generated VI names. Default `ReoLox` → `ReoLox_<Camera>_Motion` etc. Leave default unless you need a legacy `Reolink` prefix.

loxoneIntercomEnabled.label: Enable Loxone Intercom integration
loxoneIntercomEnabled.help: When doorbell rings, send the RTSP stream URL to <Prefix>_<Camera>_intercom so the Loxone Touch panel can display the camera feed.

_generateVIs.label: 📋 Generate VI list for my cameras

loxoneVIList.label: Virtual Inputs to create (events → Loxone)
loxoneVIList.help: Click ‘Generate VI list’ to fill this from your cameras. Create each Virtual Input in Loxone Config (names are case-sensitive), then F6 to save. The name already starts with the camera, so no separate column is needed.

_viSteps.text:
How to create the Virtual Inputs (step by step):

1.  Click ‘Generate VI list’ above — the table fills with the exact input names for your cameras.
2.  Copy a name from the ‘Virtual Input name’ column, or use the table’s Export button to save the whole list to a file.
3.  In Loxone Config open Peripherals → Virtual Inputs and add a Virtual Input for each row.
4.  Set its Name to the copied value (case-sensitive — paste it exactly).
5.  Type: rows marked ‘digital’ stay digital (0/1); a row marked ‘text’ (intercom) → switch the input to Text.
6.  Press F6 to save to the Miniserver.
7.  Use the inputs in your program — ReoLox pushes 1/0 (or the RTSP URL) to them in real time, nothing to configure on the Loxone side.

The same names also appear under reolox.0.<cam>.loxone.vi* after the instance starts.

loxoneVOList.label: Virtual Output commands (Loxone → cameras)
loxoneVOList.help: Create ONE Virtual Output in Loxone Config with address http://<ioBroker-IP>:<webhook port> (default 7777), then one command per row, HTTP method GET. The Miniserver IP and localhost do not need the shared secret; any other IP appends ?secret=…. A ready-to-import template is also produced as ReoLox_Loxone_VirtualOutput.xml.

loxoneVOXml.label: VO template XML — copy, save as ReoLox.xml, import in Loxone Config
loxoneVOXml.help: Ready-to-import Virtual Output template for your current cameras. Select all → copy → save as a .xml file → Loxone Config: Peripherals → Virtual Outputs → import. Address uses the Webhook tab’s ioBroker IP and port.

_voSteps.text:
How to create the Virtual Output (step by step):

1.  Click ‘Generate VO list’ for the command table, or ‘Generate VO import XML’ for a ready-to-import file.
2.  Fastest (import): copy the XML field above, save it as a .xml, then in Loxone Config → Peripherals → Virtual Outputs → import. Done — skip the rest.
3.  Manual: in Loxone Config add a Virtual Output and set Address to http://<ioBroker-IP>:<webhook port> (default 7777).
4.  For each row add a Virtual Output Command: paste CmdOn into the command-on field and CmdOff (if present) into command-off; HTTP method GET.
5.  Analog rows (e.g. brightness) contain <v> — Loxone inserts the value; mark the command as analog.
6.  Press F6 to save, then wire the commands to buttons / logic in your program.
7.  From the Miniserver IP and localhost no shared secret is needed; from any other host append ?secret=… to each command.

The Export button on the table saves the command list to a file.

_loxoneInfo.text:
Virtual Input naming convention

Create these inputs in Loxone Config (names are case-sensitive). The prefix is configurable above; default ReoLox.

ReoLox_{Name}_Motion — motion detected
ReoLox_{Name}_AI_person — person (AI)
ReoLox_{Name}_AI_vehicle — vehicle (AI)
ReoLox_{Name}_AI_animal — animal (AI)
ReoLox_{Name}_Online — camera online (1/0)
ReoLox_{Name}_Visitor — doorbell pressed (1/0)
ReoLox_{Name}_gate_trigger — gate trigger pulse (1)
ReoLox_{Name}_intercom — RTSP URL string on ring (Loxone Intercom)

The exact VI names per camera are visible in reolox.0.<camId>.loxone.* states after the instance starts.

webhookEnabled.label: Enable webhook server
webhookEnabled.help: Start a local HTTP server that receives push events from Reolink cameras — no polling needed for doorbell and visitor events.

webhookPort.label: Listen port
webhookPort.help: Port cameras POST to — must be reachable from the camera network.

webhookHost.label: ioBroker IP (visible to cameras)
webhookHost.help: Used to auto-configure each camera's push URL on startup.

webhookSharedSecret.label: Shared secret (recommended)
webhookSharedSecret.help: If set, every webhook POST must include `?secret=…` or X-ReoLox-Secret header with this value. Auto-configured push URLs include it automatically. Stored encrypted.

webhookIpAllowlist.label: Source IP allowlist
webhookIpAllowlist.help: `auto` accepts the configured camera IPs. Combine it with explicit IPs if needed, e.g. `auto, 192.168.0.175`. Control commands (/reolox/cmd) also always accept localhost (127.0.0.1).

controlApiEnabled.label: Allow Loxone control commands (HTTP)
controlApiEnabled.help: Lets a Loxone Virtual Output drive any control state directly via this server: GET /reolox/cmd/<state.path>/<value>. The Miniserver IP (from the Loxone tab) is trusted automatically; the shared secret above still applies. No simple-api adapter needed.

_webhookInfo.text:
**How it works**

When ioBroker IP, port and shared secret are set, the adapter automatically sets the push URL on each camera at startup.

Cameras POST to:
`http://{ioBroker-IP}:{port}/reolox/{CameraName}?secret=****`

Events handled: **visitor** (doorbell button), **motion**, **person**, **vehicle**, **animal**.

The server validates:
  • POST method only
  • path must start with `/reolox/`
  • source IP must be in the allowlist (auto-derived by default)
  • shared secret matches (constant-time comparison)
  • body ≤ 64 KB (oversize requests get HTTP 413).

**Manual setup** — if auto-config fails or firmware is older:
Camera web UI → Alarm → Push → set URL to the address above.

**Control from Loxone (no simple-api)**

With *Allow Loxone control commands* on, a Loxone Virtual Output can write any control state:
`http://{ioBroker-IP}:{port}/reolox/cmd/{Camera}.control.whiteLed/1?secret=****`
Analog (Loxone inserts `<v>`): `…/cmd/{Camera}.control.whiteLedBrightness/<v>?secret=****`
NVR channel: `…/cmd/{NVR}.ch3.control.recording/0?secret=****`
Allowed from the Miniserver IP (Loxone tab) or the allowlist; only `*.control.*` states are writable.
